notes.title: Back into Battle DLC Release
notes.content:
Welcome back, everyone!

We, that is Alter Games and Daedalic Entertainment, are proud to announce and release the first DLC "Back into Battle" for Partisans 1941 - and you don't even have to wait any longer - it's out now!

[previewyoutube=lJgbaT0Amrc;full][/previewyoutube]

The “Partisans 1941 – Back Into Battle” DLC allows you to customize and approach missions in your own way in Missions Mode. Choose from five familiar missions (available for everyone) and seven brand new missions (exclusively for DLC Owners), then set yourself a challenge with the modifier system. Create your dream team of Partisans, then customize and outfit them freely to suit your strategy. Use this new freedom wisely: the new challenges will be a real test of your skills as Partisan commander!

On top of that, the DLC introduces “Heroic Defense” mode. Overwhelming enemy forces, scarce resources, one Partisan position to defend: How long can you hold the line in this all new, tough as nails wave-defense mode?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36754876/c951fe395b3cd7b61ceaaefdcee861247079fa5f.png[/img]

[b]Features[/b]
[list]
[*] Sandbox approach for high replayability
[*] Missions Mode: Brand new challenges in 5 familiar and 7 new locations
[*] Customize scenarios with modifiers. Freely choose your Partisan team, skills and equipment
[*] Heroic Defense mode: New wave-defense mode for the toughest of commanders
[*] Additional camp fire dialogue for the Partisans, giving you new insight into their personalities 
[/list]

notes.title: Player Feedback patch
notes.content:
Heyho everyone!

...Wow!...What a release! After an already great first weekend the interest and passion gamers all over the world have shown for Partisans 1941 is overwhelming - but we can’t be too overwhelmed, we still have a job to do:

We appreciate all your love for the gameplay, but also the bugs and issues you have brought to our attention during the last 2 weeks. We immediately started to tackle a lot of those with our first patch after the first weekend. And we promised to keep it up. We might not have eradicated every last bug there is yet - but we are on a good path...

These are the changes and fixes that we were able to compile into todays patch:

[u][b]Some changes only apply if you start the mission again from the base.[/b][/u]

[b]General Fixes:[/b]

Now it's possible to rebind all the in-game buttons.
Fixed problem with blocked partisans right after mission starts.
Doors are working better now.
Fixed possibility to shoot through doors.
Fixed amount of bullets in the weapons after player places it into the warehouse.
Improved enemy cone of view visualization.
Fixed problem with blocked partisans, who were sent to perform any activity at camp.
Patrol with a dog now reacts correctly after dog's death.
Mines and traps can now be placed on the corpses of enemies.
Fixed an issue with impossibility to save on "Execution" mission.
Increased noise radius while shooting pistols.
Fixed Steam achievements.


[b]Partisans balance fix:[/b]

- Belozerova's ability "Fan fire" now has increased radius of shooting. Decreased max distance of ability using.
- Belozerova's ability "Evasion roll" now has increased distance of roll. Strongly decreased cooldown of ability.
- Sanek's ability "Disguise" now can't be activated during combat.
- Nikitin's ability "Massacre" has decreased max distance of ability using.
- Morozov's ability "Whistling" radius is strongly decreased. Ability cooldown is decreased.
- Different abilities which affect character speed now can be saved correctly (for example "Strength" or "Sprinter").


[b]Other fixes and improvements:[/b]

- Russian voiceover now is set by default.
- Different art improvement on maps.
- Decreased loading time.
- Localization.

notes.content:
Heyho everyone!

The first weekend with Partisans 1941 released to the public was a blast - even though some of us might have had less sleep than usual, it was needed that we can be there for you in the first hours and days whenever questions arose. We couldn't be more thankful for the amount of feedback you have been bringing in.

Because of this we already have a good overview about the sharp edges that some of you are still having issues with at the moment - which means we can focus now completely on solving them, to make the game as great as it can be!

[b]As a reminder we would like also to mention that savegames from other pre-release versions like the demo, closed beta or even the pirated review version are not compatible with the release version (and following ones) and can cause unexpected issues .[/b]

Unique Partisan abilities got improved and related issues fixed:

- Buckshot (Trofim) now also affects enemies behind cover

Further polishing and improvement regarding:
- Art
- Localization
- UI
- Remnants of debug menu got removed

Please be advised that this patch does not cover all issues reported until now. But we are working hard to provide further improvement patches very soon.


[i]Important![/i]

If you have start-up problems please go to our [url=https://discord.gg/Db2Wxqd]Discord Server[/url] and check the channel #crash-on-startup-bug - this way we can funnel the problemsolving into one area - thank you

notes.title: Partisans 1941 is out now, bringing real-time Commandos tactics to the Eastern Front
notes.content:
Over the past two years or so, World War II games have cast their gaze more frequently onto the Eastern Front, focusing in on the German invasion of Russia and the counteroffensive that eventually saw the Red Army press the German Army all the way back to Berlin. Partisans 1941, out today, is a tactics game set in the invasion that puts you in charge of a plucky band of Russian patriots using guerrilla tactics against a larger and more well-equipped occupying force.

If you remember the Commandos games, or the more recent Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, you'll have a pretty good idea of what Partisans 1941 is all about. It's a real-time game, and you'll want to carefully use stealth, traps, and well-timed ambush tactics to gain the advantage on the occupying Nazi forces.

Along the way you'll recruit new resistance fighters and develop your team's skills, resting up and leveling at a secret camp. Our esteemed colleagues at The Wargamer have a Partisans 1941 review out now and they've come away fairly impressed, noting in particular the satisfaction that accompanies a perfectly executed tripwire trap and ambush.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Partisans 1941 is Available Now!
notes.content:
We are proud to be able to declare Partisans 1941 as officially released!
Partisans 1941 is a real-time tactics game set on the eastern front of World War II. It features tactical squad combat, stealth elements, character progression, and resource management. Take control of Partisans, a brave group of resistance fighters, opposing the Nazi occupation behind enemy lines. Every mission must be carefully planned and initiated to overcome the enemy. 

Recruit soldiers and civilians as unique allies to tackle a variety of challenges – from focused sabotage to extensive attacks on German supply lines. The expandable home base deep in the forest with different types of buildings serves as the Partisans’ hub in-between missions to arm and upgrade their own troops, manage and distribute resources, and take a break until the next objective awaits. Form a Partisan group to your liking and send them on autonomous tasks or take them into battle.

Be a part of the community!
We are highly  interested in your thoughts about the game - this is why we have set up a Discord Server for our most active community members. Here you can share your tactics, report bugs, give feedback directly to the developers and publisher and discuss everything about Partisans 1941 with other fellow gamers. [url=https://discord.gg/Db2Wxqd]Partisans 1941 Discord[/url]
Disclaimer: Partisans 1941 is a game - no political statement. We want to guarantee that you can fully enjoy our game to its full extent, which is why we will delete any political discussion on our community platforms without any further comment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36754876/d012e643192bdb0091648c888e2d1e9a10015258.jpg[/img]

Core features:
A fresh approach to the tactics genre: A mix of combat, stealth, ambushes and a variety of special items brings chaos to the enemy ranks. Choose your own way of completing each mission.

Lead a squad of partisans: Find, recruit and level up new resistance members to build the squad of your choice. Use your characters’ strengths to find the right solution to different situations. 

Experience the life of a resistance group: Experience a partisan’s routine in between missions - develop your base, prepare for the next assignments, ensure you have the resources for the partisan’s survival and keep your troops motivated. 

A different perspective on WWII: Experience the story of a fierce resistance against the German occupation on the Eastern Front. Follow the stories and motives of various people who join the partisan forces – from soldiers to common folk.

notes.title: Partisans 1941 Review
notes.content:
So, you may not have heard, but way back when in '41, some not so great guys called 'Nazis' invaded the USSR. This made the local people pretty irritated, and some of them started bushwhacking the Germans during their occupation. It's some thrilling and poetic stuff, and it's surprising that there haven't been any games based on it (that I know of) until Partisans 1941 came around.

Reminiscent of the pretty good Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, Partisans is notably more action focused. Where in Shadow Tactics, a wrong step would get your guys killed pretty quickly, in Partisans you can actually have gun fights against the Nazis and not get instantly owned.

So how does a real-time stealth-action game translate to the Eastern Front?

LIKE DEFIANCE (2008) BUT LESS DEPRESSING

The story follows one Commander Zorin, a Red Army officer, who is captured by the invading German forces, but manages to escape in the first level, which is good because this would be a very short game otherwise. On Zorin's way out, he stumbles into one of his men and a local boy, who takes the group to a hideout in the swamp. This hub can be upgraded in between missions to allow your soldiers to forage for more food, customize weapons, and go complete off-map operations to get more resources, among other tasks. The hub isn't particularly deep, but it does offer a nice extra layer to the real meat of the game: the missions.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Partisans 1941 review
notes.content:
Partisans 1941 review
Partisans 1941 is the Commandos formula put through a WW2 Soviet filter, and it’s a great piece of work. It’s less flashy than the similar Desperados 3, but makes up for it with a nifty base management metagame, and an immersive, Russian-written setting.

  • Developer: Alter Games
  • Publisher: Daedalic Entertainment
  • Release: 14 October 2020
  • On: Windows
  • From: Steam
  • Price: £TBC/€TBC/$TBC

Valya, my sniper and occasional medic, kicks things off. Having chloroformed a sentry, she’s now sat snug in his position, with a great view of the SS officer commanding the checkpoint. Crack – her rifle (it’s our only decent one) fires, and his head bursts. On the other side of the position, Captain Zorin leaps from a bush preceded by a hurled knife, under the arc of an improvised grenade lobbed by his old mate Fetisov. The knife thuds into a forehead, while the grenade lands squarely at the feet of the man on the heavy machine gun. He has no chance of getting away in time. Neither do the other two troopers impeded by the sandbags of the gun nest.

Two more nazis do manage to leap from the blast, and cluster up with three other bewildered SS. They are just drawing their aim on Zorin, backing into cover, when a woman marches out of a door behind them. She has a stolen luger, and she is very fast. Five bullets go into five backs, and five bodies start to fall. Before they hit the cobbles, Valya fires a second shot at the penultimate survivor, and Zorin drives his spare knife into the last. I send the brigade sprinting for cover, but there’s no need: the fight is over. They’ve just killed 12 heavily armed fascists in five seconds, and I’ve just fallen slightly in love with Partisans 1941.

notes.title: Questions and Answers
notes.content:
Heyho everyone,

What an amazing wave of interest - We are glad that presenting Partisans 1941's Demo was a great success for all parties involved - you got some great game time and we got some great feedback!

We are at the moment in our final period before releasing the game, which is why our development team at Alter Games and our publishing team here at Daedalic Entertainment are putting all of their effort into finalizing the release.

This obviously doesn't mean, that we are not reading every post or message you are sending our way - only answering them one-by-one individually becomes a bit more difficult during this time of production.

To counter this, we selected some of the most frequent asked questions from the steam forums and tried to answer as good as we can at this point in time:




[h3]
When is it going to be released?[/h3]

As written on our store page of Partisans 1941 we have aimed to release "Summer 2020" and it looks so far like everything is going like planned, so that we can release the game end of this season. We hope to announce a precise release date soon.



[h3]Are you going to have Win7 support? [/h3]

This is a bigger topic, that we keep on discussing further internally - but generally it is extremely difficult to maintain support for a system that the creators themselves have stopped supporting. We just don't have the capacity at the moment to deal with inevitably upcoming difficulties with those versions, as additionally, if we were to support Win7, we (in context of fairness) would have to support other out-of-date systems, as well.



[h3]What about censorship? Is it going to be worldwide, or maybe different versions for different regions?[/h3]

Again, a bigger topic - You are correct, that in germany, where Daedalic Entertainment is based, the law about the depiction of this kind of symbols was updated recently - Unfortunately when releasing/publishing a game worldwide, though, there are multiple juristications we have to care about.
And even if all the countries would allow it generally, we are working together with multiple partners to ensure a favorable release - partners that could have very different internal rules or perspectives on what they want to advertise and promote. 
Since there are so many various opinions about this topic - ranging from historical authenticity to the opposite spectrum, that asks, why we should give that ideology (in combination with their symbols) anymore "stagetime" in any shape or form - we need to discuss this topic further internally. 
One of the already discussed ideas could be an optional setting - but this would surely have to wait until after release and would have to be checked beforehand, if this is even possible.



[h3]Is it going to be released on the consoles? PS4, Xbox One etc.[/h3]

As with most titles of Daedalic's portfolio, we are always trying to reach as many players on as many plattforms as possible. Eventhough for now the release on PC is our focus, this means that we are looking as well forward into the future to Partisans 1941 on consoles.



[h3]Any other shops? GOG, EGS?[/h3]

This will be basically the same answer as for the console question - the more, the merrier! 
The only difference is, being connected to our PC release as well - so you can expect news on this regard earlier than news on future console releases.




Thanks for your attention and your already great support - we can't wait to release and show you what we got prepared for you! Stay tuned for more infos!

Best Regards - Alter Games and Daedalic Entertainment

notes.content: Thinking about making a U-boat game? Unless you’ve some quirky new angle or have a mind to model WWI U-boats my advice would be don’t. The genre is as rammed as a freshly sealed sardine can at the moment. First-time devs Iron Wolf have the right idea. Instead of following their well-reviewed co-op board game about Kriegsmarine convoy molesters with a PC take on the same subject, the Polish outfit is aiming to spellbind simmers with a game played from a convoy chaperone’s perspective.
